item.title: Exclusive cross section measurements of $^{12}$C(n,p$_\text{n}$) and $^{12}$C(n,d$_\text{n}$) reactions
item.description: arXiv:2611.16075v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A single-crystal chemical vapor deposited (sCVD) diamond detector was used at LANSCE to measure neutron-induced reactions on carbon. Neutrons with a broad energy spectrum were produced via spallation. Relative cross sections are reported from above threshold up to 26 MeV incident neutron energy for $^{12}$C(n,p$_2$)$^{12}$B, up to 23 MeV for $^{12}$C(n,p$_{3+4}$)$^{12}$B, and up to 35 MeV for $^{12}$C(n,d$_1$)$^{11}$B and $^{12}$C(n,d$_2$)$^{11}$B, all of which represent the highest-energy measurements for these reactions to date, and the first measurement for (n,d$_2$). Cross sections for $^{12}$C(n,p)$^{12}$B$_\text{total}$ and $^{12}$C(n,d)$^{11}$B$_\text{total}$ are also reported from sums of the partial cross sections. These measurements are compared with recent data from EXFOR as well as TALYS calculations. These data are useful for future nuclear data evaluations and can be used as cross section inputs for data-based simulation packages.

item.title: Observation of the $\Lambda(1520)$ suppression in Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.02$ TeV
item.description: arXiv:2611.17010v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A suppression of the baryonic $\Lambda(1520)$ resonance yield relative to the $\Lambda$ ground state by $0.589 \pm 0.015^{\rm stat} \pm 0.086^{\rm syst}$ is observed in central relative to peripheral Pb-Pb collisions, with a significance of $6.8\sigma$. The $\Lambda(1520)$ production at midrapidity is measured in six centrality classes in Pb-Pb collisions for the first time at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.02$ TeV with ALICE. The $\Lambda(1520)$ is a sensitive probe of late-stage hadronic interactions since its lifetime is comparable to that of the hadronic phase in heavy-ion collisions at the LHC. Statistical hadronization model calculations, predicting yields at chemical freeze-out, overestimate the measured ratio. The transverse-momentum spectra and the centrality dependence of the suppression are reproduced by the MUSIC hydrodynamic model only when coupled to the SMASH hadronic transport afterburner, which implements rescattering and regeneration in the late hadronic stage. The measurement, which represents the first observation of resonance suppression within a single collision system, provides a stringent test of the late-stage dynamics and evidence that hadronic interactions substantially modify reconstructible resonance yield.
item.dc:creator: ALICE Collaboration

item.title: Tau polarization, new physics and CP violation in $\nu_\tau$-nucleus hyperon production
item.description:
arXiv:2611.15252v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Charged-current interactions of the $	au$ neutrino are the least constrained sector of the Standard Model (SM) flavour structure, and the polarisation of the produced $	au$ lepton probes new-physics (NP) couplings, including CP-violating ones. Hyperon and charmed-baryon production gives access to the $u	o s$ and $d	o c$ transitions, but any measurement would be made on nuclei, which calls for a proper treatment of nuclear effects. We therefore study the sequential reactions $
u_	au\,{}^A Z	o	au^-(	o\pi^-
u_	au)\,\Lambda_c^+ X$ and $ ar
u_	au\,{}^A Z	o	au^+ (	o\pi^+ ar
u_	au)\,\Lambda X$ within the impulse approximation. The energy and angular distributions of the pion, which encode the $	au$ polarization, are derived for an arbitrary nuclear hole spectral function. As for free nucleons, an azimuthal pion asymmetry with respect to the plane spanned by the neutrino and the outgoing baryon is shown to remain. This is a CP-odd observable that vanishes in the SM, so that a nonzero value would signal CP violation irrespective of the hadronic form factors. Local Fermi gas results for ${}^{16}$O show that nuclear effects lower the reaction thresholds but leave the pion distributions, and hence the polarization information, close to their free-nucleon form. For representative NP scenarios the predicted asymmetries are at the percent level or below, with a magnitude that, in the $\Lambda$ channel, depends strongly on the transition form factors.
item.dc:creator: E. Hern\'andez, J. Nieves, J. E. Sobczyk

item.title: Development of millikelvin scintillation photodetectors with CUPID
item.description: arXiv:2611.15593v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: CUPID is a next-generation tonne-scale cryogenic experiment that will search for the neutrinoless double beta decay $(0\nu\beta\beta)$ of $^{100}$Mo. It will be located at the Gran Sasso National Laboratory (Italy) and will employ the cryogenic calorimetric technique to reconstruct the energy deposited in Li$_{2}$MoO$_{4}$ crystals, in which the isotope of interest is embedded. Preliminary measurements have been performed with the CUPID VSTT (Vertical Slice Test Tower), a prototype tower designed to test the detectors' response and the apparatus' mechanical and thermal stability. In addition, a key objective was to demonstrate the improved performance of germanium-based cryogenic light detectors. In CUPID, light detection is used for both particle identification and pile-up rejection. Li$_{2}$MoO$_{4}$ is a scintillating crystal, enabling particle identification by exploiting the dependence of light yield on particle type. This requires collecting the Li$_{2}$MoO$_{4}$ scintillation light, peaking at $\sim$600 nm, with a $\sim$300 $\mu$m-thick high-purity germanium wafer placed next to the crystal. The wafer is also equipped with concentric Al electrodes biased at a few tens of volts. This bias improves the signal-to-noise ratio by an order of magnitude thanks to the Neganov-Trofimov-Luke effect. This work presents preliminary results on the performance of the VSTT light detectors and of its Optical Injection System.

item.title: Probing gluon saturation with forward heavy-flavor correlations in proton-nucleus collisions
item.description: arXiv:2611.15897v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate heavy-flavor azimuthal correlations as probes of gluon saturation in high-energy $p$+$p$ and $p$+Pb collisions within the Color Glass Condensate effective theory. Heavy flavor has several advantages: heavy-quark production is especially sensitive to the small-$x$ gluon distribution of the target, while the quark mass suppresses collinear radiation. Further, the heavy meson carries a large fraction of the momentum of its parent quark, so that the meson pair follows the partonic kinematics more closely than for light hadrons. We present the first calculation of heavy-meson pair correlations over the full azimuthal range that combines small-$x$ evolution from an initial condition constrained by HERA data with Sudakov resummation near the back-to-back limit. It provides a good description of the $D$-$\bar D$ and $b$-hadron pair correlations measured by LHCb. In contrast to the light-flavor case, we predict, in addition to a suppression of the away-side yield in $p$+Pb relative to $p$+$p$ collisions by about $15\%$, a broadening of the peak by approximately $10\%$ to $25\%$ for Gaussian fits near $\Delta\Phi=\pi$, which makes heavy-flavor correlations a promising observable in the search for gluon saturation.
item.dc:creator: Farid Salazar, Bj\"orn Schenke, Wenbin Zhao

item.title: Relating Short Range Correlated Pair Abundances to Electron-Scattering Cross Section Ratios
item.description: arXiv:2611.16489v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We derive a coupled set of relations between inclusive and semi-exclusive nucleon-knockout electron-scattering cross-section ratios measured for any two nuclei in short-range-correlation (SRC) kinematics and the microscopic neutron-proton, (np-), proton-proton (pp-), and neutron-neutron (nn-) SRC pair populations in those nuclei. The derivation uses a factorized description of quasielastic scattering from SRC pairs and includes final-state interactions through nuclear transparency and single charge exchange. We show that the inclusive $(e,e')$, proton-knockout $(e,e'p)$, and neutron-knockout $(e,e'n)$ ratios are not independent: for any two nuclei where one is isospin symmetric ($N=Z$), two of these three observables determine the third within the model. For $^\mathrm{48}\mathrm{Ca}$ and $^\mathrm{40}\mathrm{Ca}$, for example, the measured inclusive $(e,e')$ and proton-tagged $(e,e'p)$ ratios predict $^\mathrm{48}\mathrm{Ca}/^\mathrm{40}\mathrm{Ca}(e,e'n)=1.35\pm0.07\,(\mathrm{exp})\pm0.15\,(\mathrm{model})$. A measurement of the $(e,e'n)$ ratio therefore provides a direct consistency test of the factorized pair-counting description. It also constrains the single-charge-exchange probabilities. Combining all three ratios with the two double-coincidence ratios determines the relative np-, pp-, and nn- SRC pair populations of any two nuclei. If one nucleus is isospin symmetric, any two of the three ratios suffice for the same result.
item.dc:creator: Ilay Wischnevsky Shlush, Igor Korover, Eli Piasetzky

item.title: Probing the internal structure of the $\Omega\Omega$ dibaryon via its weak decays and lifetime
item.description: arXiv:2611.16508v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The weak decay properties of the $\Omega\Omega$ dibaryon play a crucial role in probing its internal structure and guiding experimental efforts. Using an effective Lagrangian approach, we systematically study its weak decays and lifetime by computing the widths for both three- and four-body final states, with amplitudes receiving contributions from single- and double-weak-vertex diagrams. We investigate the dependence of the decay properties on the binding energy ranging from a few MeV to over $100$ MeV. For weakly bound states ($E_b = 1$ and $20$ MeV), the three-body channels $\Omega \Lambda \bar{K}$, $\Omega \Xi \pi$, and $\Xi \Xi \bar{K}$ exhaust essentially the entire width, with the largest channel shifting from $\Omega \Lambda \bar{K}$ at $E_b=1$ MeV to $\Omega \Xi \pi$ at $E_b=20$ MeV. For deeply bound states ($E_b = 100$ and $120$ MeV), the $\Omega \Lambda \bar{K}$ channel is forbidden, and the dominant modes are $\Omega \Xi \pi$ and $\Xi \Xi \bar{K}$, while the double-weak-vertex channel $\Lambda \bar{K} \Lambda \bar{K}$ is found to be negligibly small. As the binding energy increases, the total lifetime extends from the order of $10^{-10}~\mathrm{s}$ to $10^{-9}~\mathrm{s}$. These distinct differences in decay patterns and lifetimes provide valuable theoretical reference values for experimental searches at RHIC and the LHC, and offer a clear discriminator between the compact hexaquark and weakly bound molecular interpretations.
item.dc:creator: Qi-Fang L\"{u}, Deng-Wang Tang, Yu-Bing Dong, Peng-Nian Shen, Jia-Jun Wu

item.title: Three-body dynamics of the Roper resonance
item.description: arXiv:2611.17139v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The enigmatic Roper resonance is notoriously difficult to determine in lattice QCD. Its quantum numbers, $J^P=1/2^+$, allow for two pions and a nucleon in relative $S$-waves. This absence of a centrifugal barrier leads to strong three-body $\pi\pi N$ effects on top of the two-body $\pi N$ channel -maybe the reason why the Roper is obscured in lattice QCD close to physical masses. Guided by unitarity, an amplitude is constructed in which three-body states are populated through channels in $f_0(500)N(939)1/2^+$, $\pi\Delta(1232)3/2^+$, and $\pi N(1440)1/2^+$ configurations. The latter channel is required by unitarity in the presence of nucleon exchange, and it contains the nucleon as a bound state, generating the $\pi N$ channel automatically. With the sub-channels matching the corresponding two-body amplitudes from experiment and nucleon properties, the $P_{11}$ amplitude from SAID is fitted, allowing for an accurate determination of the Roper poles close to the complex $\pi\Delta$ threshold. The Roper poles and residues are, for the first time, determined by explicitly including this and other non-analyticities in combination with strict two- and three-body unitarity. Contour deformation allows for a direct pole search. Systematic uncertainties from the parametrization dependence are quantified. The result for the Roper $S$-matrix pole is $\sqrt{s_R}/{\rm MeV} =1346\pm 2^{+6}_{-3} - i(81\pm 2^{+7}_{-8})$. The amplitude developed here will serve as the central input for a quantization condition that allows for future determinations of the Roper resonance from lattice QCD.
item.dc:creator: Jinzi Wu, Michael D\"oring, Maxim Mai

item.title: The Gator low-background spectrometer: readout upgrade and photomultiplier tube radioassay for XLZD
item.description: arXiv:2611.17187v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We report on a readout upgrade of Gator, a low-background high-purity germanium spectrometer operated at the Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso for material radioassay. The upgraded data acquisition records digitised waveforms, enabling noise rejection on an event-level basis, and offline energy reconstruction. Measurements before and after the upgrade show an improved energy resolution of 17% at the 2614.5 keV line of 208-Tl, with (2.14 +- 0.22) keV at FWHM, and suppression of electronic noise in the low-energy region. We assess the resulting sensitivity for a specified sample geometry, and present a new background measurement. The background rate in the (100-2700) keV range is (86.6 +- 0.5) counts/(kg day). We also show the radioassay results of sixteen Hamamatsu R17317 3-inch photomultiplier tubes with an improved stem design, which reduces the activities from the primordial 238-U and 232-Th chains by a factor of three, making them suitable candidate photosensors for the XLZD experiment.
item.dc:creator: Laura Baudis, Sofia Calgaro, Jose Javier Cuenca-Garcia, Florian Joerg, Margherita Noia, Francesco Piastra, Aravind Remesan Sreekala

item.title: Jet-like di-hadron correlations in pO, OO, and Ne--Ne collisions
item.description: arXiv:2609.24237v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Heavy-ion collisions are primarily studied to investigate the properties of hot and dense nuclear matter, known as the quark--gluon plasma (QGP). However, recent observations of hydrodynamic flow-like behaviour in pp and p--Pb collisions at the LHC suggest the possible formation of QGP droplets even in small collision systems. To bridge the multiplicity gap between small and large systems and to examine the applicability of hydrodynamic descriptions, light-ion collisions were performed for the first time at the LHC in 2025. This contribution presents measurements of the near-side peak width of di-hadron correlations in pO, OO, and Ne--Ne collisions with ALICE, used to search for medium effects. The width of the near-side correlation peak is studied as a function of the average charged-particle multiplicity at midrapidity. At low transverse momentum ($p_{\rm T}$), the near-side peak is broader in OO and Ne--Ne collisions than in pp and pO collisions, and in central collisions its width approaches that measured in Pb--Pb collisions. At higher $p_{\rm T}$ the peak narrows modestly with increasing multiplicity. The results are compared with PYTHIA, AMPT, and JETSCAPE calculations, none of which reproduces the measured widths over the full kinematic range.
item.dc:creator: Suraj Prasad for the ALICE Collaboration

item.title: Space-time Areas and Hadronization Studies
item.description: arXiv:2508.05784v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Space-time area laws play a fundamental role in modeling strongly interacting phenomena, such as in relativistic string models, QCD on the lattice, and in hadronization modeling. For the latter, an exact expression for relevant space-time areas related to the final state hadronic events for hadrons of any mass is calculated. Usage of this expression in the UCLA hadronization model helps validate its space-time area law (STAL) principle and unifies the treatment of heavy and light hadrons via a single fragmentation function.
item.dc:creator: S. Abachi, C. Buchanan

item.title: Corrections to the Smoothness and On-Shell Approximations in Femtoscopy and Coalescence
item.description: arXiv:2602.02810v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Relativistic heavy-ion collisions produce femtometer-scale sources whose space-time structure can be constrained using two-particle femtoscopic correlations. Standard implementations rely on the smoothness and on-shell approximations, which effectively remove the relative momentum dependence of the particle emission function. We explore the validity of these approximations by deriving model-independent expansions that quantify the leading corrections for femtoscopy and coalescence with arbitrary sources and final-state interactions. The resulting first- and second-order correction terms can be evaluated with essentially the same numerical complexity as the usual Koonin-Pratt expressions; for angle-averaged correlations the first-order contributions vanish by symmetry. This version of our paper corrects a numerical error in a previous version. We find that the smoothness corrections are numerically larger than previously reported.
item.dc:creator: Isaac G. Smith, Kfir Blum

item.title: Sequential Bayesian inference with correlated heavy-ion datasets
item.description: arXiv:2605.17868v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Bayesian inference provides a natural framework for updating knowledge as new information becomes available, often in a sequential manner by incorporating datasets in stages or reusing previous posteriors as priors. A common implementation uses a factorized update in which datasets are treated as conditionally independent. When datasets have statistically correlated uncertainties, however, this approximation generally becomes inconsistent with the joint likelihood and can lead to distorted posterior constraints. In this work, we investigate this issue in a controlled setting using pseudo-data with a tunable covariance structure. We compare joint inference, factorized sequential updating, and a formulation based on the exact conditional likelihood. We show that factorized updates reproduce the joint posterior under conditional independence, but develop systematic deviations when correlations are neglected, with discrepancies that increase with correlation strength in our numerical examples. In contrast, conditional sequential updating reproduces the joint posterior exactly. To interpret these deviations, we introduce an information decomposition that separates the joint information into contributions from the first dataset and the conditional information provided by the second. By comparing marginal and conditional information, we show that correlations induce structured changes in the constraints on different parameter combinations, reflecting the interplay between covariance structure and dataset sensitivities. This information-based analysis provides a quantitative interpretation of the observed posterior discrepancies. These results provide a practical diagnostic for assessing the consistency of sequential Bayesian inference with correlated datasets and highlight the need for a consistent treatment of correlations within a common probabilistic framework.
item.dc:creator: Lipei Du
